title: Parameter estimation of a whole-brain model with a hybrid physics-informed neural network
topic: Hybrid PINN estimation of MPR whole-brain model parameters from resting-state fMRI
lema: The two configurations of the same MPR model are compared on the same data after a synthetic test of discriminability; to the authors' knowledge no earlier study does this.

novelty.central_idea: Regional excitabilities of a whole-brain MPR model from one subject, with the regime decided by the data
novelty.novelty: Bistable against monostable configuration of one biophysical model on real resting-state fMRI
novelty.novelty_detail: The two configurations of the same MPR model are compared on the same data after a synthetic test of discriminability; to the authors' knowledge no earlier study does this.
novelty.problem: Regime-assumed estimates of regional excitabilities $\eta_i$, of unknown reliability, in whole-brain MPR models fitted to single-subject resting-state fMRI
contributions: Regime decided by the data along a noise grid
Noise-aware PINN as transversal estimator and reconstructor of slow regional states
Zero-mean noise forcing tied to the noise level

equations.heading: 4. Method
equations.latex: (\hat r_1^*,\dots,\hat r_N^*,\hat V_1,\dots,\hat V_N) = \mathrm{NN}_\varphi(\tilde t), \qquad \tilde t = \frac{2t}{(T-1)\,\mathrm{TR}} - 1, \qquad t\in\left[0,(T-1)\,\mathrm{TR}\right]
equations.connection: where $\varphi$ are the network weights, the time domain runs from the first to the last volume, $\hat r_i^*=\tau_m\hat r_i$ is the dimensionless rate of Section 5, and a softplus on the outputs $\hat r_i^*$ keeps the rate positive.

equations.heading: 4. Method
equations.latex: \eta_i = \eta_0 + a\,m_i, \qquad \eta_0 = -4.6 + \sigma_\eta\,\tilde\eta_0, \qquad a = \sigma_a\,\tilde a, \qquad G = G_0 + \sigma_G\,\tilde G
equations.connection: where $m_i$ is a fixed regional map, standardised to zero mean and unit variance over the $N$ regions and declared in Section 3.1, so that $\eta_0$ is the mean excitability and $a$ its gradient along the map (Kong et al. 2021; Zhang et al. 2024).

equations.heading: 5. Loss function
equations.connection: Each term is dimensionless, and any scale it is divided by has a meaning defined by the problem, never a value taken from the current state of training.

equations.heading: 5. Loss function
equations.latex: \mathcal R_{1,i} = \frac{d\hat r_i^*}{dt^*} - \left(\frac{\Delta}{\pi} + 2\hat r_i^*\hat V_i\right), \qquad \mathcal R_{2,i} = \frac{d\hat V_i}{dt^*} - \left(\hat V_i^2 + \eta_i - (\pi \hat r_i^*)^2 + J\hat r_i^* + G\sum_j A_{ij}\hat r_j^* + u_i(t)\right)
equations.connection: where the derivatives come from automatic differentiation with respect to the network input, with $d/dt^* = \tau_m\,\frac{2}{(T-1)\,\mathrm{TR}}\,d/d\tilde t$ by Eq.
